title: Slab-packing & progressive-fidelity KV-cache study (FP8/INT8/INT4)
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Investigate a slab-packing storage layout and a progressive-fidelity fallback policy for KV cache entries to reduce GPU memory footprint while preserving generation quality and latency SLOs. The study will measure FP8/INT8/INT4 encodings across slab sizes, eviction heuristics, and continuous-batching interaction points. Primary goals: map quality degradation vs memory savings, identify safe switching thresholds, and produce an automatic rollout plan with regression gates.
background: We currently store KV cache in a contiguous per-shard buffer with per-request allocations. Previous experiments focused on per-vector quant schemes and blockwise compaction, but fragmentation and continuous-batching amplification lead to uneven memory pressure and tail latency spikes. Slab-packing (fixed-size allocation buckets) may reduce fragmentation and make low-bit encodings more deterministic. Progressive-fidelity means encoding entries at higher precision first and degrading older/cohort-less-critical entries to lower precision according to a budget policy.
success_metrics: Reduce peak GPU KV cache usage by >= 30% on 90th percentile production traces
Maintain median generation latency increase <= 5% and 95th percentile increase <= 15%
No regression in token-level perplexity on internal prompt set > 0.8 delta
Embedding cosine drift <= 0.02 for reranking/eval tasks when compared to baseline
A/B stable rollout with <1% of requests flagged for immediate rollback
experiment_plan: Implement slab allocator for KV entries with slab sizes [128, 256, 512, 1024] element vectors
Integrate three encoding pipelines: FP8 1-block, INT8 asymmetric, INT4 block-interleaved with per-slab scale metadata
Add progressive-fidelity controller that tags entries by age, token-cohort (inferred from route), and recency score
Simulate continuous-batching traces offline (1000 production trace samples) to measure fragmentation, compaction throughput, and latency impact
Run microbenchmarks for forward pass throughput and kernel selection overhead when decoding different encodings
Stage canary in Dedicated with 10% capacity and shadowing for 24h before A/B rollout
Collect quality signals: log-prob delta, sampling divergence, downstream eval scoring (QA F1, summarization ROUGE surrogate)
Gate rollout on quality and latency thresholds, with automatic fallback to higher-fidelity encodings per-model if thresholds violated
observability_plan: Per-slab memory occupancy metrics (by slab size & encoding)
Tail latency and queueing time per batch size
Kernel switch count per-request and cost per-token breakdown
Alerting on sustained quality drift or >10% increase in failed completions
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: INT4 encoding causes catastrophic token errors for specific attention patterns. Mitigation: keep fast rollback and require model-specific fidelity thresholds; run targeted fuzz tests on long-context prompts.
Risk: Slab allocation increases copying overhead during compaction. Mitigation: benchmark in-proc memcpy vs pinned GPU-to-GPU copies and limit compaction frequency to low-load windows.

Risk: Continuous batching interacts poorly with mixed encodings causing kernel fragmentation. Mitigation: add batching-aware scheduler that groups same-encoding requests or limits mixed batches to a small fraction.
Risk: Unexpected interaction with KV eviction policy leading to high cache churn. Mitigation: simulate with synthetic churn patterns and add backpressure to slow writes when churn > threshold.
